utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I just want to inform both parties that we might have to sit this afternoon because we lost two days of the other week and we tried to find time to make it up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now we are in the open session now. Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Will you please make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper the usher is showing to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Examined by Mr. Bos:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: We do. Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, the usher is going to show you a sheet of paper, and on that sheet of paper is your name and the name of the pseudonym which the Trial Chamber has given to you. Could you please look at this paper and confirm that this is indeed your name, which is on the paper?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you can see on the sheet of paper, the pseudonym that has been given to you is Witness NN, double "N." From now on, I will refer to you as Witness NN. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, where did you live before the war started?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: At Zegulja, municipality of Stolac, the village of Orlja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is your ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Bosniak Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell me what happened on the 18th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: On the 18th of June, I was expelled by the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you go to after you were expelled?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: I went and my old mother went with me towards Stolac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Stolac?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Three days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go next?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: The Chetniks then started to shell Stolac, and orders were given by the civil defence to have the civilian population moved towards Capljina and other places, including Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So where did you go then?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: We went to the village of Oplicici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, did you try to join the army to fight the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Yes. We went several times to report to the HVO, the TO, and the HOS; however we were turned down because of a lack of weapons and equipment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But is -- is it correct that at one moment, you did join an army?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: On the 5th of September, I joined the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain why you joined this army and not any other army?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: At that moment, when I had this wish to sign up because my -- because our country was occupied and because they had taken my uncle prisoner, who was a close family member.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you stationed in the Bosnian army?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: We were at the southern camp. And then the Croat Defence Council did not allow us into their zone of responsibility. I noticed even before that that the Croat Defence Council was not something that we would be doing together. As was said before, there were chequer-board signs, flags, pictures of Ante Pavelic, on the MUP building, the municipal building, and other buildings. It was obvious they were not in favour of the BH. And in my opinion, they were in favour of some kind of Herceg Bosna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What makes you say that that you felt that they were in favour of some kind of Herceg Bosna, the HVO?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, because there weren't any flags of Bosnia-Herzegovina, et cetera. There were only chequer-board flags.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does a chequer-board flag represent?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, you see, of course, this was a symbol of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened on the 13th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: On the 13th of June, 1993, in the village of Rotimlja, which was in our zone of responsibility, we received orders from our superior command that we should withdraw towards Blagaj, that there should be no conflict with the Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened when you withdrew?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: We were arrested by the Croat Defence Council. This is the road leading to Blagaj, and it's called Grab.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many people of you were arrested?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, about 40.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you surprised about this arrest?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, of course we were. There were between 100 and 200 soldiers there, the special unit called Bozanovi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time in Rotimlja was there an armed conflict between the HVO and the Armija?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did they take you and your fellow soldiers?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: I and my fellow soldiers were taken to the neighbouring village of Medjine. We were there, and they brought in three other soldiers of ours. And it's the -- it's the first time that I heard the greeting "Za dom spremni," "It is for the homeland," three times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does this greeting mean?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Later on, I found out that "Za dom spremni" is the Croatian greeting. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how this greeting was given?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, if you were to ask me what my name was, I would say I don't know. They would say "Za dom," and we would have to reply "Spremni." And that happened three times. "It is for the homeland." Answer: "Ready."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they do anything physically as well, or was it just --

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: No. Two men were singled out there, and they were supposed to negotiate, reach a compromise, that there should be no shooting, that they would let us go, that we'd go home, that our families and some women were even detained at a school in Crnici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did they take you then?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Then they took us in a Zastava truck towards Capljina, to Gabela.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you taken in Gabela?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Gabela? We were lined up by the wall of a garage, and we were robbed there. And I saw Dzemal Topic there, and Senad Bilali, nicknamed Leki there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, is Gabela, was that a prison facility?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, it was a camp. If you saw camp inmates there, it was a camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see any prisoners in this camp when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, yes. I just told you; those two I mentioned. And then they took us into a garage made of tin, and then they took us out again, and then we had to do push-ups. And they asked Bajro Pizovic, the commander of my brigade -- I could barely recognise him because he was all black and blue. He was arrested sometime before that in April 1993. So that shows how badly he was beaten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you just before you mentioned two names, who were these persons you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Names? Oh, they were some members of the army. They were arrested before us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you give a rough estimate of how many prisoners were already in the Gabela camp when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: I could not give a number. I'm just telling you that I saw these two men, and also this commander, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For how long did they keep you at the Gabela camp?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: About three or four hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you taken next?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Onto a bus. They told us that we were being taken for an exchange. But that was not the case. We were taken to the Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is you with all your 40 fellow soldiers who were all taken to the Heliodrom, or was the group --

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- smaller --

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Part of our group was kept in Gabela. Kemal Balavac, Mustafa Beso, nicknamed Muta.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I want you to refer to names, I will ask you.

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It may be that we -- there may be issues of confidentiality, so please don't refer to names unless I specifically ask you. Is that okay?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: All right. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So with how many soldiers did you actually -- well, with how many people were you taken to the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, about 35, 30 approximately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you taken when you arrived at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: We were taken to solitary confinement cells.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the name of the building where these solitary confinement cells were placed?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: The central military investigation prison.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay in these solitary confinement cells?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: The night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to clarify, because you said you were arrested on the 13th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it also correct that you arrived at the Heliodrom on that same date, that whatever we discussed was all happening on one day?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: All of it happened the same day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said you were -- you stayed for one night in that solitary confinement cell. Where were you taken the next day?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Yes. The next day, they took us to the attic, to the top floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any other prisoners in the attic of this building?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, yes, yes. In those rooms, there were even some women below us, actually, and they saved us. The International Red Cross came then, and they found us upstairs and we were registered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean when you say that these women saved you?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, there were quite a few inmates there who had been in the camp for half a year, and they were even released from the camp without being registered with the International Red Cross at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But -- well, that still doesn't really answer my question. Why do you think that you were saved by being kept in the attic? Is it because --

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: No. Because on that day, the International Red Cross registered us, and regardless of whether I would survive or whether I would get killed, I would be registered there and people would know that I had been there. I mean it's the Red Cross that saved us and these prisoners who told them that we were up there, told them about us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is it your testimony that the prisoners told -- some other prisoners told the Red Cross that you were kept in the attic of that building and it was not the guards who told the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Oh, no, no way. Not the guards. It's the prison inmates who told the Red Cross that there were other prisoners there. There were those who were working elsewhere, and the Red Cross were looking for these people who were in other locations, were being hidden, et cetera, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, who guarded the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: At the moment when we were brought there, and until the very end, it was the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did the military police, did these guards tell you who had actually arrested you and had taken you to the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, the police did not contact us at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would they tell you who had arrested you?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, it's like when we were going to work and things like that. Sometimes they said that we were arrested by General Juka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why would they say that you had been arrested by General Juka?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Because probably Juka was a Bosniak and at that time he was at the Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But were you in fact arrested by General Juka?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: No. We were captured by the Croat Defence Council - I told you - the special unit called Bozanovi, and there were well-known soldiers there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this General Juka, do you know his full name?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, I saw him once. And other prisoners said to me, "There is Juka." I never saw him before or after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, we saw Juka through the bars, and he went with a group of soldiers to the building below us. Tall, skinny, and with a limp, and they said, "That is this Juka."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I asked this question before, but you didn't answer: Do you know his full name?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, I guess it's Juka Prazina, something to that effect. I don't know really.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, while were you in the Heliodrom camp, did you ever see any HV soldiers or soldiers from --

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell me -- could you tell me about that a little bit more? Did you see any specific units, and how did you know that these were HV soldiers?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, there were differences between their emblems, the HV and the HVO; there was a big difference. And then also in their behaviour, and then also in terms of their technical equipment. There was a significant portion of technical equipment, their mortars, tanks, motor vehicles, the 110s, all of this from the former JNA. And through the other inmates who worked for them several times. There was the Tigers, the Zagreb unit, the Karlovac unit, and others, and Gromovi as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether these HV soldiers also participated in combat in the area?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, yes. They were always used, wherever there were these actions, and they even went to Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Vakuf is a -- which village do you mean by that, the name Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, there are two Vakufs actually. And then the HVO and the army -- probably Doni Vakuf, the lower Vakuf. I don't know. And then it's from the Avijaticarski Most, further on, towards Tresnje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I object to this question because the witness is being asked to guess, especially about places in Bosnia, and this has nothing to do with the indictment. The indictment pertains to Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I won't pursue the matter, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So you may skip this question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, did these HV soldiers had a -- had a patch which was different from the HVO soldiers?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: The HV and the HVO, there is a difference. The army and the HVO, again, there are different emblems and there is an obvious difference.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the obvious difference?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, it would say the "HV," and then it would say the "HVO."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did these Croat soldiers, these HV soldiers, did they at all times wear their HV patches while you were at the Heliodrom, when you saw them?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: No. Because we told the Red Cross there were other members of the military too. When we said that, they found out, and they changed all the emblems into one and the same emblem, the HVO. And also licence plates, HVO; those that belonged to the Croat Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, I'd just like to clarify this answer. You say the Blank pages inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts – Pages 5881 to 5893. prisoners told the Red Cross about the presence of HV soldiers? Is that what your testimony is?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened after that, when that -- this was reported to the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: They probably found out about it then, and then they didn't want to have proof of another army being present there, and then they changed the emblems, and they were all the same, so if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I have two objections: One, I object to a fact witness speculating. And that's what's happening in this case right now, speculation. Two is, in the interest of saving time, the Prosecutor doesn't need to repeat answers in the question. The witness gives an answer, and the Prosecutor repeats the answer again. In the interest of time, those are my two objections, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: May I respond to this objection?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: First of all, I thought the answer was not clear enough, and that is why I tried to clarify what he had actually said. And if that involves some repetition, then I'm sorry. But I thought the answer was not clear enough, and that's why I did this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we believe that it is kind of repetition of your question. If you -- there are certain points you are not quite clear, you may ask questions about that point, but not repeat the whole question from the very beginning to the end. And secondly, we don't believe that is kind of speculation on this time. You may -- well, I think we have to break at this moment. And here is a clarification from the Bench about the sitting plan today. First of all, we have to tell the Prosecution that we are not going to hear next witness after this one, this present one. We will adjourn until whenever we finished with the present witness. If we could finish with him by the lunchtime, there is no sitting this afternoon. But if we couldn't finish with him by 4.00 this afternoon, we might sit even longer. We will resume at 11.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bos.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness NN, for how long did you stay at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: I stayed there from the 13th of June, 1993, until the 19th of March, 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While at the Heliodrom, were you ever taken out for labour?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how often were you taken out for labour?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, that depended.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean that depended? Depended on what?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Sometimes for an entire day. Sometimes for two days. Sometimes three days running. Once I spent 15 or -- to 20 days doing forced labour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was this, this time that you spent 15 to 20 days of forced labour?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: That was in Vojno, Bijelo Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were the conditions working in Vojno? Can you briefly describe that?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Very bad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of work did you have to do?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Trenches, pontoon bridges across the Neretva River, bunkers, digging holes for rifles in garages, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, besides Vojno, where else did you perform labour?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: At Rudnik, Santiceva Street, Bulevar, at Podhum, at the plateau, of the Heliodrom, and in Potpetak and at Aksamova's woods.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me, what kind of work did you have to do in these places? You've already described a little bit what you did in Vojno, but what type of other work did you have to do?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, in Santiceva Street, we dug some sort of tunnel. At Rudnik, we built a bunker for one PAM, anti-aircraft machine-gun. In Heliodrom, we plucked grass. At Heliodrom, we dug a trench. On the Bulevar, on one occasion we dug trenches, put up sandbags. At Podhum, we also dug trenches.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you also taken to a place called Harem in Balinovac?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Yes. We dug graves for people who were killed, and we covered them with earth later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you dug graves for people who were killed. Who were these people that were killed?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat? The interpreter didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I think you have to speak a bit more into the microphone because the interpreters have some difficulty in hearing you.

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Those were mostly graves marked "NN," which means unknown. Only two graves were marked with family names, and those -- that was the Kajtaz family, mother and child.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether the Kajtaz family was a Muslim family or a Croat family?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, it was probably Muslim, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this woman and child, could you see how they were killed? Could you see --

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: I saw women killed either with a bullet or with a blunt object, that I saw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you now specifically referring to this woman you've been referring to as Kajtaz or women -- or another woman?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: I mean her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did you find out from other prisoners if they were taken out for assignments other than the ones you performed?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, yes, we did. It was this group of mine with whom I worked, and then behind me there were more people, but I don't know the names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear from other prisoners where they would work? Did you find -- did you find out if there were other places where also labour was performed, where you didn't go but where some other prisoners did go?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Yes, yes. They were taken to do work at Buna, at Varda, Rosne Njive, that is, Rosne Fields, all the way up to Ravno, as far as I heard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you recall a prisoner by the name of Salko Zolj?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he tell you about labour, what type of labour he had to do?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: He had been taken with a group away for about 20 days, and then he came back. He said he had been to the commander, Tuta, at Siroki Brijeg. He said they had been building some sort of villa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You referred to a man by the name of Tuta, the commander. Did you ever -- did you ever see this man?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you recall a time that you were given a blue uniform at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was this?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: On the 1st or the 2nd of July. Around that time, 1st of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you the only one who was given a blue uniform?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: No. There were about 20 of us, and they named us the Blue Orchestra there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know why you were given these blue uniforms?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, all of us had been members of the BH army, and it was probably for the sake of being registered somehow, identifiable, sort of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you sometimes perform labour with this group called the Blue Orchestra?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: If I can go into private session for one question, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well go into the private session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, was there an occasion that you and this group that you called the Blue Orchestra were taken to an area in Mostar near Liska Park?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It was at the Bulevar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recall approximately when that was?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, approximately, it was around mid-August most probably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you -- could you tell us who took you that day from the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: I don't know the names, but it was a member of the HVO. He had no rank insignia that I could tell. He was a commander of some sort.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did they -- where did this man take you?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: He took us from Heliodrom to the Rondo, where we got off the bus. And then we walked by the Liska Park. And then in the neighbourhood, around the health centre, we stopped. That's where the location was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And with how many prisoners were you on that day?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: 18 or 19. That's how many men we were in the Blue Orchestra.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were taken to a building. And then who was there at the building?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: You mean to whom the unit belonged? I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you said you were lined up in front of a building.

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any soldiers present at that time?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Yes. There was the man who brought us, and a woman, plus the commander. And others said it was one of Stela's commanders. I don't know his name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you say that this was a man -- could you describe this man who you say that was -- that he was one of Stela's commanders? Could you describe him physically?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: He was tall. We did not dare to look at him carefully. We were ordered to look down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have any physical remarks, except that he was tall?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, after he beat me up, he told me, "Look at me." He had a scar on his head, and he said he had been wounded by the army, and he showed another scar from a wound and his leg, and he said, "I got this from the Chetniks."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you said that were you beaten up by this man?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Yes, he was -- he beat me up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he do? Where did he beat you?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: He kicked me in the stomach, and he punched me on the head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened after that?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: After that, the following happened: After this commander was finished with me, Stela showed up, in a jeep.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you said that this man called Stela showed up in a jeep. Do you know what the colour of the jeep was?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: No, because we were looking down, as I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe this man which you called Stela?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: I can, because he beat me black and blue too. He was wearing a base -- a cap with a short hair cut, not very tall, and stocky.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you just said that he beat you up as well. Could you tell me exactly what happens so -- he arrives with his jeep, and then what happened? Could you please describe the situation?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: He got out of the jeep, and I don't know whether it was at that moment or after the match was finished, but he said, "You will find out who Stela is." He started kicking me on the head, and at that moment, I passed out. And one of the inmates asked for help, and he walked up to him. And then I noticed that he had this rubber circle to train your hand. And with this in his hand, he punched him, and he cursed his mother. While a woman was singing at that moment, "The smell of lillies is spreading across the field." And he said, "Die, you motherfucker."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, a few questions. First of all, so he first started to beat you; that's what you testified. Did he beat you also with this device which you've been talking about, or did he beat you just with his fist?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: He was punching me and kicking me. He wasn't using any objects. I don't want to lie.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did he -- where did he hit you?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: On my head, on my chest and in the stomach.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that he then -- that somebody else -- that he beat somebody else as well. Do you know the name of that person he beat after he had beaten you?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Maybe we can go into private session so that he can give the name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, while you were beaten, you said that there was this woman who was singing a song. First of all, who was this woman?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: They said it was the secretary of Stela, the commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: I don't know her name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said she was singing something about lillies. What kind of song was she singing? What's the meaning of that song?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, I don't know, but there is this song which is sung often, "The smell of lillies is spreading across the fields," and it's probably an allusion to the BH army, of which we had been members. And it was part of the emblem, together with the flag, of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what did this Stela do after he had beaten this second person?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: He said, "Go to work, and whoever won't work will be reported to me." And we were taken away then, and I never saw him again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after that, were you actually -- were you taken for work after that? And where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Towards the health centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of work did you have to do that day?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: We made loopholes for rifle fire, aimed at BH army positions, and across the Basca we made a bunker.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how long you worked on that day?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, until 8.00 p.m., approximately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were then taken back to the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, was there another occasion that you were taken to the Bulevar, to the health centre?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Yes, we were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall when that was?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: I think it was the 17th of September.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which year?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell us what happened on that day. First of all, at what time did somebody come and collect you from the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Around 4.00 a.m. We arrived up there near the health centre. We reckoned that we were going to work again. But unfortunately, it was something quite different. It was a real tragedy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With how many people were you taken there? With how many prisoners?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: We were about eight or nine. At moments like that you don't even know your own name for sure, let alone how many people there are.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit 14.3?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all before we continue, Witness, is it correct that you have some problems with your eyesight?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this something which is a recent problem, or did you have that problem as well when you were performing labour during the war?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: It all happened maybe during the time I spent at the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Maybe the witness can be shown first the photograph right -- placed in front of him so that he can have a better look at it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise what's on the photograph, Witness NN? Would you place your finger on a certain spot on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is it where you've put your finger on?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Can you mark the health centre on this picture to help me find my way around? It's difficult. I can't see very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, Witness, if this is too difficult for you, we will do it without the photograph.

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: It's difficult, really. I can't manage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, Witness. We'll do it without the photograph.

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe where you were taken that morning, on the 17th of September?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, up towards the Liska Park, and then towards the health centre, and then that area over there, between the health centre and towards the high school, over there. I mean if we were there, I could describe it for you in detail.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you put in a particular place in that area?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: We were in garages then. Later on, we found out that this was an attack against BH army positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell the Court what you were ordered to do and how this attack proceeded.

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Yes. The attack started around 4.30, 5.00. They didn't manage to break through the front. Our task was to get the wounded and the dead out, and if they were to break through the front line, that we should go as the second or third echelon and take care of the lines, fortifications, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're talking about a second and a third echelon. What was the first echelon supposed to do?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, the first echelon was prisoners, and they were going in front of the soldiers who were in action. I heard that they were even using some wooden rifles. I have to be quite honest. I did not see them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's your testimony you were in the second group; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you have to do?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, we had to pull the dead and the wounded out, if we managed to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, tell me what happened. Did you actually -- did you go out, and what did you see, and what happened?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: We got out, after the fire ceased. I met a prisoner who was getting a wounded person out, who I knew real well. And another wounded man was with him?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Maybe again, just to be on the safe side, we can go into private session so that I can ask the names of these persons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, during this operation, did you see whether any prisoners got killed?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Yes. I saw Pajo Enes lying in a pulled of blood. I don't know whether he was killed or whether he was wounded, and he was from my unit. And I saw many soldiers and prisoners lying there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, tell me what happened. So you were there and saw all these people. And what did you do?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: We were taken back from there to a different place where we were supposed to work, and that was Podhum.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, how long did this whole operation last?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: You mean action? Combat?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, approximately -- well, you know, being so afraid, it seemed to me that it went on all day. But perhaps this operation lasted about an hour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was the operation successful?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No territory was gained on that day?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that after that, you were taken to Podhum; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Yes, yes, the same day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you have to do there?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: The same: Communication trenches, through gardens from building to building, and also opposite Podhum there were sandbags. The road was closed off that way so that it could be crossed without the other side seeing you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, was there also an occasion that you worked - I think you already testified to that - that you worked at the Santiceva Street?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us when that was and for how long you worked there?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: I was there for two days and a night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was the commander at that time while you were working there?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: I don't know who the commander was, but I know who took us. And I saw that he had part of the responsibility, and that was Zelenika. Ivan was his first name, I guess. He was nicknamed Zela.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what kind of work did you have to do for this man Zela?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, this tunnel I was telling you about that we had dug behind, behind the prison, towards the positions of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and also going from one building to another.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many prisoners -- while you were working in Santiceva Street, how many prisoners were working there?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Three, and I was the fourth one. I mean we were the ones digging that tunnel, but there were always quite a few prisoners around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, while you were working at Santiceva Street, were you able to identify the insignias of the soldiers who were there in that area?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, this ATG of this military police and then this HVO, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you say ATG. Was that written on the insignia, or how did you know that the soldier was from an ATG?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, they say that that's an anti-terrorist group. This Convicts' Battalion, whatever, that's what these witnesses were saying, that's what I heard, that that is what they were called.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise any people who were there serving under an ATG?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you give me the names?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: That's Miro Stankovic. Then Ivica Dzakula, and Kulas. I know that that is his last name, but I don't know his first name. And also Bozo Peric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just looking at the transcript to see whether the names appear correct on the trip. Could you just spell the name of Dzakula

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Dzakula, Ivan. D-z-a-k-u-l-a.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Your Honour this finishes my examination.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Cross-examination? Mr. Meek, please. Cross-examined by Mr. Meek:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness NN.

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My name is Chris Meek, and I am one of the attorneys for the accused Naletilic. You mentioned an individual --

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And frankly, Your Honours, I don't know -- I don't think we were in closed session at the time he mentioned -- we could go into closed session, to be sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness NN, do you recall approximately what month it was that you had this conversation with Salko?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, believe me, I wouldn't know the month, but approximately after all these events that I mentioned previously.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it would have been -- the last events you mentioned, Witness, were -- was the 17th of September, 1993. So would it have been after that time?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, after that time, October or November. It wasn't really important to me to remember exactly when.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when this individual, Salko, told you that he had been working on a house, he had just come back from that work; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know -- can you describe this individual for the record?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: The man was taller than me, thinner, and he also wore a moustache.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After October or November, 1993, did you have any further occasions to speak with this Salko, or was this --

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the next question I would ask you would be just for yes or no. Do you know if he is alive presently?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: I see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Could we go into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The only question I would have for you, Witness NN, would be: Was any -- were any other person or persons present at the time that Salko told you this story?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, you see, when a prisoner would come back from work, alive and well, then we were expecting to hear what they'd have to say. There would be other prisoners there. But unfortunately, I don't know the names, because often I didn't know what my own name was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your direct testimony, Witness NN, you testified as to the conversation or statement Salko made to you that he had been working on a house in Siroki Brijeg. Is that the extent of what he told you, or did he go into any details?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: No, no, not on a house. It was Tuta's house. And that nobody touched them, did anything to them, and they could eat and drink as much as they wanted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was the extent of what he told you? He did not go into detail in regard to exactly what type of work he was doing, or was it inside, outside, that sort of thing?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: I could not talk about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it that he did not tell you, or you do not want to talk about it right presently?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: He did not tell me, and I do not wish to talk about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Witness NN, thank you very much. And best of luck to you.

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: You're welcome. To you, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Par, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Par

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. NN, I'm Zelimir Par, attorney at law, and I'm one of the Defence counsel for Vinko Martinovic, Stela. I'm going to put a few questions to you related to these events that you mentioned today during your testimony. Please, do you know in which unit Vinko Martinovic, Stela, was? Do you know the name of this unit? Do you know anything about this unit?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you perhaps know one of the soldiers from that unit?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the zone of responsibility of that unit at that time?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, as I heard from the other witnesses, wherever it was necessary, that's where the zone was. However, in my opinion, it was there at the Bulevar, this zone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that day, the 17th of September, 1993, do you know in which unit you were?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: What kind of unit could I be?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mean where were you brought as a prisoner?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, they told us that we were brought to Stela's and that Stela dressed many soldiers and that there are still many people who are alive, and if they are honest men, they will come here and speak the truth before justice and the truth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, during your testimony, I noticed that you stand behind what you personally saw and experienced. So my questions are primarily directed at your personal experience. And of course there were other witnesses before this Court, and there will be other witnesses, and they will talk about their experience. So please understand my questions in that way. I am primarily interested in your personal experience, knowledge, et cetera, so I hope you appreciate what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, in order to clarify where the witness was, what zone this could be, I would like to show a map, and I think it's going to be better for the witness to handle that map. I understood that the witness had some trouble with finding his way in a map but perhaps that map was inappropriate, if the witness's eyesight is troublesome. I'm going to show map 14.5, where the health centre can be seen better, the one that the witness asked for a few minutes ago. So we are going to show him this map and ask him whether he can orient himself better in that particular map.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm going to object. This is a photographer which is practically similar to the one I showed, and Your Honours yourself could see how many difficulties he had with identifying the photograph, so I really don't see the need of putting the photograph again to the witness. I don't think he will recognise anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we believe that we should let Mr. Par to have a chance to try his luck.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I think that it's the witness who really could have answered, not to have this kind of suggestion made to him, "I imagine the witness will not be able to recognise this." Your Honours, this is a very important matter for this Defence, where this event occurred on the 17th of September, because this event occurred all over the Bulevar and we are interested in which unit was involved, and we have no other way of establishing this than through a map. So again I'm asking the witness whether he can find the health centre in that particular map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. NN, can you orient yourself in this map? Can you see whether the health centre is on this map?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, it was approximately here, here, here. Here is the health centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we put this on the ELMO, please?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Oh, this is really hard for me to see. Oh, I can't tell you more than this. Impossible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you or can you not orient yourself on this map?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: The more I look at it, the more troubled I am, and I cannot really define anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you wear glasses?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: No. Doctors won't let me because of my blood pressure, because when I put glasses on, then my blood pressure goes even higher, so, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This eye ailment of yours, does it have a name? Do you have a diagnosis? Can we know what this is?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to see a doctor for these eye examinations? Did the doctor tell you what this was? Are you short-sighted, far-sighted, pressure in the eyes, anything?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: The doctor told me that this was incurable and that I should monitor my blood pressure and if it's all right, it's all right; and if not, that's the way it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you made a solemn declaration today. Did you manage to read those letters, or did you learn it by heart?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, it's different when you go letter by letter, and this was quite short, and that is one thing. And then a photograph in different colours is a different thing. I don't even drive my own vehicle because of that, let alone other things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't want to bother you with this any more, but just tell me when did these problems of yours start? A year or two ago? Ten years ago?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: I noticed them after I got out of the camp, enormous difficulties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Then about this position, because we are not in a situation where we can use a map, we'll try to do with words to discuss distances and so on. Sir, we are now interested in the 17th of September, 1993. Was it across the length of the entire Bulevar, the entire line of separation that the operation was carried out?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, from the health centre to the high school was as far as I could see. I can't say about the area beyond that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the other side of the health centre - because if you I agree with me, the health centre is somewhere in the middle of the Bulevar - and to the left and right of it, was the line of separation. So did the operation take place on both sides of the health centre? Was there shooting? Was there combat?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then we'll try another question. I want to get that place where you were on the 17th. Where were you on the 17th of September when you were brought there? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: I said it was night-time, early morning, in the small hours. And I'm not a local in Mostar to be able to find my way around so easily and to know the houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you don't know, you don't know. You just have to say so. I'm not trying to force you to remember something you don't know. So did I understand you correctly that you cannot tell us where you were exactly on that day when you were brought there?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: No. I just said that we were brought to a garage, and it's a large area over there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree that it was along the entire line of separation that there was shooting from both sides during that operation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, this is really fast. And it gives a difficult time to the interpreters. Just control your pace.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I promise this won't happen again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I will repeat the question. Sir, we are talking about the operation of the 17th of September. Did it take place along the entire Bulevar, the entire line of separation?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: When we say "the Bulevar," I'm not a man born in Mostar to be able to tell, but I know that from the high school up to the health centre, there were combat operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, are you aware that at that time in that area there were several different units?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you think that this unit, Stela's unit, was holding the entire line of separation? Was that the information you had?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: I cannot say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you think that this unit, Stela's unit, was holding the entire line of separation? Was that the information you had?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: I cannot say that, I cannot speak about that, because I was not interested in knowing who held what.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear another name of another commander involved in that area on the Bulevar?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Everyone had five different names and that's what we heard when people -- different people were discussed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm trying to establish one thing. I want to prove that Stela's unit was not the only one in that locality on that day, that there were several different units in that area at the time. Do you allow for that possibility?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: I know about the existence of Stela's unit, and that's the only thing I can claim. I have no further comments.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know -- did you see Stela on that day?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who was in command of that operation on the 17th of September, 1993, on that line of separation on the Bulevar from the health centre to the high school?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We presented a document yesterday, I cannot show it to you because you cannot read it. Otherwise I would show it to you too, but I -- the Chamber knows that we presented a document which said that this operation was commanded by Mario Milicevic Baja, commander of the Benko Penovic [phoen] ATG. I want to ask you have you ever heard that name? Is it familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: No, it's not. And I wasn't interested. Perhaps if I had been there, if I had heard that name --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me once again - you told us once before but I'm not sure there wasn't a mistake - when did this attack start on the 17th of September?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: I didn't have a watch, but I reckon it was around 4.30, 5.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, again, in this brief that I just mentioned and from the testimony of several witnesses we have already heard, it transpires that the attack started at noon, at 12.00. Can you tell us, is that correct or not correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Sir, what I'm saying is correct. Let every witness tell his own truth. And I've told you this several times already, and please, don't go on and on about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may ask the Trial Chamber's leave for us to go into private session for a minute so I can ask this witness about a name?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now we are in the open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. NN, you say that your task at the time was to try to pull out the wounded and people who were killed from the line. How many persons, wounded or killed, did you see at that time, personally?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: I can say for sure that I saw those two who were wounded, this inmate Salko Gerin who was with them, and I also saw some soldiers and civilians who were lying on the ground. I don't know how many of them there were, five or six. I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And according to you, that operation finished about an hour after it started, if I understood you correctly, which means it was already over sometime in the morning, around 5.00 or 6.00. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: I'm saying again I didn't have a watch. Perhaps it was 4.00, but visibility was good, as usual. I think that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let us forget for a moment about the 17th of September, 1993, and let us go back to the event when you said Vinko Martinovic, Stela, beat you. I'm interested in the particular moment when Stela arrived. You said that he arrived in a jeep. My question is: Was Stela passing by that place and saw you stopped and got out, or how did it happen?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: We were lined up against a wall, all of us inmates, and this deputy commander of Stela's, whose name I don't know, he came up to me first and beat me up. And after he beat me up, at the same moment, this jeep appeared and he came from the other side of the building. He came up to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We know that. But I wanted to ask: Were you waiting for him?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: What was there to wait for? We were lined up there with our hands behind our backs, behind our heads, against the wall, and it was something like a boxing match with us being used as sacks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You described the event. We understand what happened to you. But I'm just trying to clarify which unit was involved.

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: I don't know anything about the unit, but I know that the commander, Stela, beat me up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll put my question again. Without going into the details of your claim, I'm asking: Those soldiers who lined you up and this man who you called "deputy commander," were they waiting for the commander, Stela, or was it that some jeep was passing by and Stela showed up and got involved in the situation?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: I don't know whether they were waiting for Stela. They are the only ones that can know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a particular reason why you were beaten up? Was there anything that could have caused you to be chosen for such treatment?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: I don't know. It's probably that I had long hair.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You think that could have been the reason?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: It couldn't have been anything else, because out of 18 or 19 of us, there was no other thing that distinguished me. We were all Muslims, we were all members of the Bosnian army. I was the only one who had long hair.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned --

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have only one more name to ask about, and then we can go out of private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now we are in the open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you are saying that there was a girl present there. Could you describe her, if you had occasion to have a look at her?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: She wore leggings. She was thin. They said she was Stela's secretary. I don't know whether that was true or not. I couldn't get a good look at her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How old was she, approximately?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: At that time, I wasn't even sure about my own age. She looked youngish. I can't say how old she was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you heard a song being sung about some lilies, and you associated that with the flag of Bosnia-Herzegovina, an allusion of some sorts?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: I didn't link that with the flag, but she was singing about lilies, and I said it was probably because we were the BH army who had lilies in their emblem. And this is a well known emblem of the BH army. And one more thing - excuse me - there is a recording of the song which is often played, and the lyrics go, "The smell of lilies is spread being across the fields."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to come back to this because somewhere in the beginning you said that the first problems that appeared during the joint operation of the HVO and the Territorial Defence started with discontent about the hoisting of those flags, the chequerboard flags. And my question is: Did Bosnia-Herzegovina had a flag of its own before independence was proclaimed?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not a politician, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know that this flag with the lilies was the flag of Bosnia-Herzegovina during the war?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Yes. I saw it and it's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I'm asking you now, is that the flag of the State of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: It's not, and please don't ask me about that. Ask me about the things for which I was called here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were the one who mentioned the flag, and I'm not going to ask any more questions about the flag. I don't want you to get nervous. Whenever the witness does that it is the counsel who is blamed.

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: I'm not being nervous and I'm not being upset. I'm just telling the truth. I will tell the truth whenever I know it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a little while longer, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Witness, would you please keep a distance from the mike, please? Because we have some difficulties. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have just one more question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the sake of clarifying one part of this witness's testimony. Sir, you mentioned the camp of Vojno in Bijelo Polje. Could you tell us who was the warden of that camp, the commander of that camp at the time when you were there?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: At first, the commander was a man called Rudo, who was not bad, but later, it was Mario Mihalj, and his deputy was Dragan Sunjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Witness NN. I have nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any re-examination, Mr. Bos?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Witness, I would just ask you to clarify a number of issues. You described the incident where you were lined up against a wall with your hands behind your back, and you said that the deputy commander of Stela's unit beat you up. I'm talking about that incident. And you referred a couple of times to a boxing match. What did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, he was punching me so fast as if I were in the ring together with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I see. And the other thing I wanted to ask you about was you had mentioned that you didn't know Mostar very well. Did you know it at all before these terrible events in your country?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: You mean Mostar; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: The town of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Once I brought my mother to a hospital, to the internal ward, up at Bijeli Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: The reason I asked you that - and you may not know - is that you referred to a place called Liska Park.

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Did you know that or did you know anything about that area also being a Muslim cemetery?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: I didn't know anything about it, only that people were buried there during the war, but -- and there are crosses there for people of all ethnic backgrounds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: So you do know that it was some sort of a cemetery or some part of it was a cemetery?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Yes, in those years of war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you. When you talk about the war, you're talking about the war with the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Now, my final question is -- and I recognise that you say that there were times that it was hard for you to know your name, never mind numbers, but can you help us: Of your group that was first arrested by the HVO, your unit in the army - and most of you were taken to the Heliodrom, you said - how many of you survived?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, you see, I know that two men got killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: And -- of your Blue Orchestra? Is that what you're talking about? Two men were killed in the Blue Orchestra?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: No, only one man got killed from the Blue Orchestra.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: So does that mean that approximately some number in the 30s survived the camp?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Witness NN, before your arrest that took place on the 18th of June, 1992, did you know Stela?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: I was not arrested on the 18th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You were arrested when, then?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: I said I was arrested on the 13th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So before your arrest, did you know Stela?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You were not the only soldier that was arrested. You were a soldier, like all the other soldiers that were with you. Why did somebody hit you? Was it reprisals? Was it a corrective measure? Were you hit because of a bad answer given during a cross-examination? Were you punished in some way? You were not the only soldier.

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am talking about the event when you were beaten by the commander of Stela and Stela himself. I did not understand. You were not the only soldier in that group. There were other soldiers in your group. How is it that spontaneously you were hit? Was it because you had committed a mistake? Was it for corrective measures because you did not answer correctly or you didn't do a job correctly?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: No questions were asked. We were just lined up. And he immediately started beating me. And he then said, "Look at me," and he showed me that he was wounded in the head by the BH army and in the leg by the Chetniks. And we couldn't lie about our identities. We couldn't pretend that we were not military men. It was obvious we were members of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you able to recognise Stela here in this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: He hasn't changed a bit. If I were in his shoes, I would drop dead right here and now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Witness.

utterances.speaker: Witness NN
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions out of judges' questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no questions, Your Honour, but I would really have to exert some effort to refrain from asking for an explanation of such a comment that we just heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Bos?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, very much, Witness, for helping us by giving your evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, too. I am proud that I lived to see the day when I can come before this Court and tell the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And we all wish you good luck in your future.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: When the usher pulls down the blinds, he will lead you out of this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And have a nice day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are there other matters to attend to, Mr. Bos?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. There are no exhibits. R. MEEK: None for Mr. Naletilic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nothing to tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President if I could just have one more minute of the Court's time, please. First of all, I do want to thank the Chamber for its willingness to sit later today in the event -- it turned out not to be necessary, but we do appreciate the Chamber was willing to do that. On scheduling, I just wanted to inquire, because the videolink testimony is scheduled for the week after next, and we are getting to that point where we have to get serious about making the arrangements, et cetera. And I'm asking this question not to advocate a position necessarily but just simply so that we can plan properly. The days that will be taking the videolink testimony, as you probably can expect because of the time differences, will require that we start later in the day. In fact, I think at least one day I think we are going -- possibly going quite late. But I take it - and again please don't misunderstand that I'm necessarily advocating this - but during those days, we will not be working at other hours of the day, that is, we won't take other witnesses earlier in the day if we are starting, say, at 3.00 in the afternoon, I assume.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, no. We will take -- we will not take any other witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And we believe that in about ten days, we are going to hear the testimony through the videolinks in a different country. In the past proceedings, we intentionally give some latitude to both parties concerning the time they are going to use, both in direct and cross-examinations. Because of the technical problems of long distance relay, and we will start our sitting in the afternoon, perhaps until night. So we would like to invoke the Rule 90(E) to avoid undue consumption of time during the videolink testimony. Without prejudice to the rights of both parties, woe would like to invite both parties to inform the bench beforehand how long you are going to take for the direct or cross-examination, approximately. We have to finish our witness in one day so that to allow the representative of the Registrar and the technicians of this Trial Chamber to travel to another city and set up all those equipment, which means as for how long we are going to sit for one day, it all depends on you. Having said that, we will resume at 9.30 Monday morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: 1.01 p.m., to be reconvened on the 19th day of November, 2001, at 9.30 a.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
